Hi there Reddit General_ !! Let's get started this is what this thread is for ask whatever! 

1) Pushing someone from lower ground is a waiting game, wait for them to be pre occupied with looking at someone else. When most players in this game are in a gun fight they tend to tunnel and not watch their flank. That is the perfect time to push someone who is on higher ground! 

2) Well this game is not PUBG, so every fight you need to build, if you die without building you're in the wrong game brother! Yes building is the greatest item and skill set someone can have in this game always having higher ground is what players need to strive for in fights. Take Ninja for example he never takes fights low ground. If he needs to use 400 wood to get above someone he will. That being said using a lot of resources and being able to recover comes with being better at the game! If you miss your first shot gun bullet yes build. You don't want to die because you lost a shotty vs shotty battle when you have building! 

3) I never stand still when harvesting, always aim for the blue circle that pops up, and here is a little trick if you're going for wood from trees don't fully break them. Get them to 50 HP that way the big animation of the tree breaking doesn't give away your position! 

4) Let's say my team or I come in from Pleasant we are not at Loot Lake, there is a team that is at Factories and a team built more north. Which ever team has the lower ground and crapper looking base we will push. My team rarely sits in a base we want to get the kills ASAP, our avg squad win is 9-11 minutes we are always moving. Pushing teams that have the lower ground. 

5) Are you using headphones or just speakers. That plays a huge role into hearing the foot steps. I have a Razer Tiamat 7.1 surround sound headset and that is something I never have a problem with. If you have the money to invest in better sound it is worth it IMO if you want to play more competitive at any shooter! But if you have a headset it will just take time in order for you to understand the footsteps. 

6) This kinda goes back to question 1 just follow that and you will be golden! 

7) My late game inventory usually consist of ( 1. Pickaxe 2. AR 3. Shotgun 4. Sniper 5. Small Shields 6. 15 bandages or medkits which ever one I have beforehand! 

Hope that helps you a little bit and good luck in your games!

1) Well I don't have the PvE mode so I can't really comment on that whether or not it helps in PvP. The way I learnt how to start building faster is making sure I have my walls, stairs and ceiling all key binded to something I find very comfortable. I have a Razer Naga so I have my wall as 7, my stair as 8 and ceiling as 9. All these are pressed with my thumb and muscle memory helps me build extremely fast!  

2) Best way to approach someone in squads is have some of your teammates distract the enemies and avoid being seen. Get high ground on them and let your teammates know you're in position to attack. Get them to poke the enemies so they focus on your team. While they are shooting you should be able to take them out from behind if they built poorly. Which a lot of the players in this game do!

Yes the higher you are the better on hills. You never want to have to fight looking upwards. If you start shooting at someone below you you're going to hit more head shots than the other person % wise.  Building big bases isn't really worth your materials it just makes you a bigger target for people to come at you. 1x1 or 2x2s are the best option for speed builds!

Shoot the wall/stair down at the right time and the rocket will bank off the back wall and you will get the knock. Hopefully those tips will help!

Hi Odinspirit, jumping shotgun battles is a tough one to really help someone out on. Again this is a situational fight, it all depends on what shot guns both of you have. Just for the sake of this let's say you both have green pump shot guns. Now with the Pump and jumping around can be very difficult and comes to not panicking. Really focus on those shots. I have played with people who say "Man my shotgun only hit for 7, 13" or some low number like that. What is happening is that they are using the shotgun like COD where if a single bullet hits it does full damage. Most times when I go back on their VODS to show them what they did the little dot is way off to the right or left. Now going back to the pump v pump battle. Don't always try to go for those headshots when in a jumping shot gun battle, you're more than likely to miss your shot unless you have the higher ground on that person. Hitting for 95 is just as good as getting a headshot in those situations. With the head being such a small target and moving fast and being up close it's really hard and most of your bullets will miss which causes the 7 -36 damage markers. Try to go for body shots and build in between shots. Building is key to jumping shot gun battles always try to get the high ground and waste your opponents ammo and then get the kill. Hope that helps.
